resources.string: Scan the QR code a site shows when you turn on two-factor authentication, or enter its setup key. Codes are generated offline on this device. To move from Google Authenticator, choose Transfer accounts → Export there and scan its QR code here.
Point the camera at the 2FA QR code
The Base32 key shown with the QR code
The key must be Base32: letters A–Z and digits 2–7.
Most sites use SHA1, 6 digits and 30 seconds. Change these only if the site says so.
No QR code found in that image.
That QR code is not a 2FA setup code.
Camera access is needed to scan. You can choose a screenshot or enter the setup key instead.
QR code read. Check the details, then save.
This 2FA code is already in your vault as “%1$s”.
This 2FA entry is damaged and cannot make codes.
If two-factor authentication is still on for “%1$s”, you will need another backup of this key or the site\'s recovery codes to sign in.
They will be permanently removed from this vault. This includes %1$d 2FA codes: without another backup or the sites\' recovery codes, you may be locked out of those accounts.
Setup keys are left out of CSV exports; only encrypted backups include them. Keep a backup: losing this phone without one means losing these codes.
From a Google Authenticator export. They are added to your vault; nothing is replaced.
%1$d counter-based (HOTP) accounts are not supported and were skipped.
%1$d accounts already in your vault were skipped.
Nothing new to add from this QR code.
If the export showed several QR codes, scan each one.
